summary: The CLI entry guard in exp-001-stability.ts checked the module URL suffix for '.ts'. When compiled to dist/*.js the guard evaluated false, so `node dist/experiment/experiments/exp-001-stability.js` exited 0 having run nothing and written no output. This is the same defect class previously found in dr-counterfactual.ts on the VPS.
what_went_wrong: The guard pattern `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).replace(/\\/g, '/').endsWith('exp-001-stability.ts')` is only true when the module is loaded from TypeScript source. Under compiled ESM the URL ends in '.js', so the CLI branch is skipped. A caller invoking the compiled artifact receives a successful exit code and an empty/missing output file — a silent failure that could be mistaken for a valid zero-result run.
detection: Caught during a local smoke test of the compiled artifact (3 seeds) which produced no output file, before any large run was launched.
root_cause: Extension-specific guard copied from dr-counterfactual.ts, which has the same latent defect. The guard conflates 'is this module the program entry point' with 'was it authored as TypeScript'.
remediation: Changed the guard to an extension-agnostic check: `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).replace(/\\/g, '/').includes('exp-001-stability')`. Rebuilt, re-ran the smoke test (3 seeds, H=10) — produced 3 valid JSONL lines. Updated scripts/exp-001-orchestrate.py to invoke the compiled `dist/...js` instead of `npx tsx`, removing the TypeScript-runtime dependency from the execution path.
impact: No corrupted results were produced. All validation and primary runs executed through the corrected compiled artifact. The dr-counterfactual.ts instance of the same defect was already remediated earlier on the VPS.
process_lesson: Any CLI-guarded experiment script must be smoke-tested as the COMPILED artifact, not just via tsx, before a long run. A zero-byte or missing output file with exit code 0 is the signature of this failure.
